ten_clauses.name: Joint Borel actual bounce
ten_clauses.derivation: The joint gradient difference is continuous. Scalar inner product/norm/power are Borel, and total real inverse/division is Borel including zero. Subtraction, scalar multiplication and product pairing preserve measurability.

ten_clauses.name: Joint continuous actual rate
ten_clauses.derivation: Joint gradient difference, inner product and positive-part max are continuous; sqrt eta is fixed.

ten_clauses.name: Joint Borel actual rate
ten_clauses.derivation: Continuous implies measurable on the given finite-dimensional real product Borel spaces.

ten_clauses.name: Zero-normal reflection
ten_clauses.derivation: At n=0 both inner product and scalar-multiple term vanish under total division, so R(0,p)=p.

ten_clauses.name: Householder involution norm and pairing
ten_clauses.derivation: R(n,p) is reflection in (span n) orthogonal complement, not reflection in span n. Thus R squared=id and norm is preserved. For n nonzero, pairing equals a-2a=-a; at n=0 both sides vanish.

ten_clauses.name: Actual bounce fixes position and is involutive
ten_clauses.derivation: Position is unchanged, so the second application uses the same normal h(xRef,x); apply R involution.

ten_clauses.name: Exact weighted SUM energy preserved
ten_clauses.derivation: Both the center and position stay fixed, and the individual momentum norm is preserved. The exact inverse-eta weight and factor one half remain unchanged.

ten_clauses.name: Rate positivity flipped positive part and signed balance
ten_clauses.derivation: For a=<p,h>, reflection sends a to -a. Since sqrt eta is nonnegative, rate>=0 and rate(Sz)=sqrt eta max(0,-a). Identity max(0,a)-max(0,-a)=a gives the exact signed rate difference.

ten_clauses.name: Actual zero-normal bounce and rate
ten_clauses.derivation: If h(xRef,x)=0, R fixes p and the pairing and rate vanish, with no requirement p=0.

ten_clauses.name: Nonnegative energy and same-layer uniform rate cap
ten_clauses.derivation: For e=H(z0)>=0 and H(z)=e, weighted SUM gives ||p||<=sqrt(2e) and ||x-c||<=sqrt(2 eta e). Lipschitz gradient, triangle and Cauchy-Schwarz give lambda<=sqrt eta beta sqrt(2e)(sqrt(2 eta e)+||c-xRef||).

caller_audit.gradient_Lipschitz: Existing QuadraticRegularization theorem with U=V,m=alpha,L=beta,r=0,u=0; W=V and L+r=beta by simp.

boundary_audit.zero_normal: R0=id and lambda0=0, even p nonzero.
boundary_audit.zero_energy: p=0 and x=c on the same H=0 layer, hence lambda=0 even if h(xRef,c) is nonzero.
boundary_audit.rank_zero: All vectors/norms/gradients vanish; finite-dimensional completeness and reflection APIs include the zero space.
boundary_audit.alpha_eta_one: No inverse or division by 1-alpha*eta occurs; eta stays positive.
boundary_audit.Borel_vs_continuity: Actual S is only Borel; rate is continuous. Discontinuity of S at zero normal can occur even under the callers.
